text: Even when you cannot promise results because of legal disclosure rules, you can state the facts: the metrics of the open locations. The answer is to improve those metrics.
title: How to Sell More Franchises (Without Selling Them)

text: He argues that whatever makes a business unattractive to keep scaling as corporate also makes it unattractive for franchisees to buy in.
title: How to Sell More Franchises (Without Selling Them)

text: He suggests spending about 24 months going down to the penny to make the restaurant far more profitable, citing Panda Express running 27% net margins despite heavy corporate overhead.
title: How to Sell More Franchises (Without Selling Them)

text: Prefer partners with a genuine following built on personality and influence, not only looks. Their audience is loyal, and the brands they associate with signal a lot, because customers know the person rather than the founder.
title: Helping a $4.5M Clothing Brand Scale to $100M

text: Customers transfer the values they see in an influencer onto the brand that person promotes. A luxury buyer follows luxury-associated people, so a premium brand should be paired with those figures rather than mass-market ones.
title: Helping a $4.5M Clothing Brand Scale to $100M

text: Be careful about who you curate associations with, then double down. Recruit as many fitting people as possible, whitelist them to run ads, and have them run testimonial contests among buyers through their links, with giveaways, to generate UGC ads.
title: Helping a $4.5M Clothing Brand Scale to $100M

text: Bigger promises convert more people but lead to higher churn. A stronger promise lowers the bar for saying yes, yet gives buyers more reasons to leave once it ends. Promising little attracts fewer buyers who churn less.
title: How to Make Offers People Never Churn From

text: If members stay because of the owner, the owner must keep producing new material. If they stay for each other, the members generate the value themselves, so who they are staying for matters for retention.
title: How to Make Offers People Never Churn From

text: Solving a member's first problem tends to expose a next problem. If the owner is clear about what that new problem is, it becomes the basis for continuity.
title: How to Make Offers People Never Churn From

text: He says the lowest-churn communities he has seen with broadcast-style delivery use consumable deliverables. The front-end course works as a one-time system, but running it requires ongoing supplies, like ink, that members keep buying from the owner.
title: How to Make Offers People Never Churn From

text: For a broadcast-style community where the owner provides the value, he recommends blending education with fresh news or data that keeps changing, since members return for it. This is less relevant when members deliver value to each other.
title: How to Make Offers People Never Churn From

text: When serving small businesses, price low enough that they do not cancel in bad months, because their revenue volatility turns into volatility for you.
title: How to Scale a White Label Agency Past $1.5M

text: Small businesses are poor at running their business, which tempts agencies to do more and more of the work for them. Hormozi says this misses the point: they are weak customers, so you must price very low or high enough that they cannot afford you.
title: How to Scale a White Label Agency Past $1.5M

text: Agency-style services for small businesses can reach one to three million dollars a year in revenue through grinding, but the revenue does not stack without some form of retention.
title: How to Scale a White Label Agency Past $1.5M

text: For a distributor-based business, the key problem is keeping most agencies referring business every month. If about 80% remain next year, revenue compounds year over year instead of resetting.
title: How to Scale a White Label Agency Past $1.5M

text: When building a distribution layer, he uses a two-part approach that begins with a launch to get an immediate win, since a new distributor has not yet had time to see value.
title: How to Scale a White Label Agency Past $1.5M

text: For paid search style PPC leads, speed matters above everything: contact the lead by double dialing and texting within 60 seconds, or a competitor wins them. For Meta leads, about 5 minutes is tolerable.
title: \"Can I Scale Without a Sales Team?\"

text: There are many ways up the mountain and all channels can work. What matters is choosing one and sticking with it, such as LinkedIn content, outbound to centers of influence, or PPC.
title: \"Can I Scale Without a Sales Team?\"

text: He describes an affiliate-style approach, partnering with people who already own the customer base, as a supply-side version of the same strategy, working the same way.
title: \"Can I Scale Without a Sales Team?\"

text: The order for fixing growth is offer first, then sales motion, then traffic.
title: \"Can I Scale Without a Sales Team?\"

text: A business relying on referrals or content usually has a warm-traffic offer that only works on people who already know the company. Growing requires converting this into a cold acquisition process, which he says applies to most people.
title: \"Can I Scale Without a Sales Team?\"

text: Hormozi says the most valuable use of a founder's time is closing deals, so list your tasks, keep promoting and closing as the top two, and get someone else to handle everything else.
title: \"I Built a Team of 12. Why Am I Busier Than Ever?\"

text: When handing off client coordination, he suggests framing it to the client that the founder stays in the close where he adds the most value, while a named colleague handles the details.
title: \"I Built a Team of 12. Why Am I Busier Than Ever?\"

text: Every entrepreneur has to buy their time back, and the process never ends. Once you get time back, you must make more money with it than it cost to buy.
title: \"I Built a Team of 12. Why Am I Busier Than Ever?\"

text: The longer he has been in business, the more he weights intelligence when hiring. He wants very smart generalists, who he says can usually figure things out quickly.
title: \"I Built a Team of 12. Why Am I Busier Than Ever?\"

text: He says a lot of unnecessary process gets created when a team has lower-intelligence people, and new hires should raise the bar of the team.
title: \"I Built a Team of 12. Why Am I Busier Than Ever?\"

text: If one person on your team drains your time and you wish they would vanish, remove them even if they perform, because the founder is the highest revenue generator and their time matters most.
title: \"I Built a Team of 12. Why Am I Busier Than Ever?\"

text: Nearly every successful person he has met went through many years, not just a month or a year, of unrewarded work, doing boring things and giving up appealing ones for their main goal. He calls this the Rocky cutscene, lasting 5 to 10 years.
title: How to Outlast the 10-Year Grind Before You Win

text: Everything worth doing is hard, and a bigger payoff comes with bigger hardship. He says that if something is hard, that is good, because it means others will not do it.
title: How to Outlast the 10-Year Grind Before You Win

text: He thinks much of entrepreneurship and personal growth is training how you respond to hard. Early on he treated hard as a warning sign to slow down, stop or pivot.
title: How to Outlast the 10-Year Grind Before You Win

text: Once he was clear on the path and saw obstacles as dragons to slay for the treasure, he became happier the harder things got, since no one else will follow. He calls it a selection effect.
title: How to Outlast the 10-Year Grind Before You Win

text: When a founder is bored because the business runs without them, Hormozi suggests spending all their time on outreach to recruit salespeople who can sell more of the company's offering.
title: “I Run Soccer Tournaments. How Do I Scale?”

text: Real authenticity is being honest about the deeper truth, not surface-level truth. Most people are afraid to do that, and instead adopt a ready-made personality without customizing it.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: He likens authenticity to aftermarket modifications on a stock personality: everyone has a body and brain, and what matters is what you chose to do with them, and committing fully to that.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: People become interesting through apparent contradictions or uncommon pairings, such as a muscular man who discusses philosophy. When someone breaks the expected pattern, observers realize their assumptions were off and want to learn more.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: He suggests a partner or spouse should hold something interesting that you did not expect, and that learning more about them keeps surprising you. He also links this to attraction.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: To be interesting, show the apparent contradictions that actually exist within you rather than taking a personality off the shelf.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: He defines personality as simply what you do: how someone acts under given conditions.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: Identity is a label placed on top of your behaviors, and it then steers future behavior. Someone who identifies as a runner runs even when unmotivated; entrepreneur can mean willingness to suffer and work hard long-term.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: If your labels and behaviors are copied off the shelf, your content will look like everyone else's. AI excels at pattern recognition, so its content tends toward the average, and content that looks like content does not work.
title: You Need to Be Authentic

text: When resources are limited, he prefers doing more of the channel that already works over adding new online channels, because working online leads is a whole different challenge from a simple direct sale.
title: Helping an $810K Home Service Business Get to $3M

text: He says that once a business runs many teams, such as 15 trucks covering a city, it makes sense to add top-of-funnel awareness that generates leads plus a central phone team that sends trucks to already-sold customers.
title: Helping an $810K Home Service Business Get to $3M

text: He sees a business that sells a heavily customized build first and then offers to keep it running as a front-end and back-end model, and he expects the ongoing service side to carry very strong gross margins.
title: I Built a $1.5M Business I Secretly Hate

text: Hormozi says swinging staff up and down with the seasons is built into this type of business, and accepting that stops you wasting effort trying to solve it.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: He suggests not labeling a period on season or off season, because employees will then treat it as off season. Instead present two jobs, one for summer and one for cold months, to keep people employed.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: Every business has a hard part, and that difficulty is why owners get paid. He compares it to finding reliable cleaners in his own cleaning business.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: Weak sales motion and inability to raise prices often go together. Fix the sales motion, then raise price; with thin gross margins, a price rise of roughly 20 to 30 percent will probably be fine.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: He says most businesses like this are supply constrained rather than demand constrained, so getting workers is harder than getting customers, which makes price the easiest lever to move even though owners fear it.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: If you price and sell well, you may afford more full-time workers, which he says would stabilize the business.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: Whichever path you choose, once you win your daily life looks the same: talking to the heads of sales, field crews and billing or service, not doing the work yourself.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: When two options seem equal, he would compare LTV to CAC and choose the one where it is easier to acquire stickier, higher-value customers.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: He calls it one of the biggest business mistakes to phone poor prospects and try to sell them expensive things, then blame the business when they refuse instead of the mismatch of customer.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: He thinks a lead magnet and offer aimed at a higher-income customer, followed by a matching sales flow such as a VSL and fast lead response, would help.
title: Helping a Landscaper Scale From $1.3M to $10M

text: Hormozi holds that money is not mysterious: it is a generalized means of exchange and a unit for measuring value, and you earn it by giving value and getting something back.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: When two parties exchange value that is unequal, money makes up the difference, so he sees it as a way of balancing accounts.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: He observes that many money influencers use vague terms, mysticism, manifesting or energy talk. He suspects this is because they cannot explain money in clear, observable terms, and that rhetoric is easier than reality.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: His rule for communication is to state facts and tell the truth rather than impress people or confuse them. The hard part is telling the whole truth, all the way down.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: A trading course seller claimed he wanted to help people, but his real reason was that trading wrecked his health and life. Hormozi pushed him to admit it, since honest marketing needs that truth.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: Marketing that tells the whole truth, including uncomfortable parts, is more believable and compelling, and the whole truth is the rarest thing in advertising.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: People who lack money skills invent words that sound good but mean nothing, so followers act on a flawed model of reality and are confused when nothing earns money.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: He defines terms aggressively before making statements or answering questions, comparing it to legal agreements that begin with definitions, because communication with stakes needs agreed terms.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: When asked to be kinder, he asked what that meant. The answer was phrasing statements as questions, which cost him nothing, so he adopted it and the request was satisfied.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: Words like kindness, energy or vibe are noise until defined, and saying I'll know it when I see it means it has not been defined yet.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: To make a vague judgment such as lazy actionable, ask what the person did that led to it, until you reach an observable behavior like slow Slack replies, then request that change.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: He defines truth as observable reality and tries to use only terms describing things others can also see for themselves.
title: The One Thing About Money I've Never Said

text: Hormozi thinks that when most people say they figured out why, they have built a story they accept, which may or may not match reality.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: He concentrates on observable behavior because he finds it more predictive of both his own and other people's actions than explanations of cause.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: Life has too many variables to know them all, so he sees no need to know why and thinks he never will.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: After a relationship, list the behavior changes you kept, then check whether each helps you attract a better partner. Keep the ones that do; you need not know why they happened.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: He compares a tennis coach fixing your grip: spending the session on why you hold it that way would be pointless.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: If you can predict what happens, you know the variables and can influence them, which means you can control the system. He notes people dislike this idea.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: Pick behaviors that raise the likelihood of your goal, then arrange more good and less bad so you do them more often. What happened earlier matters only if the same variable can be reused.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: He accepts learning is enjoyable and does not object to the why search as a hobby, but he judges much narrative as mental masturbation.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: Ask whether something raises or lowers the odds of reaching a goal, since that can be known. Why cannot be known because the same circumstances cannot be relived.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: Turn vague labels into concrete behaviors, then check how often they occur. Then ask whether the behavior lowers your chance of your goal; change it if yes, drop it if no.
title: Why “Figuring Out Why” Is a Waste of Time

text: Venture investing suits tech because it needs the chance of very large exits, and the economics of tech lend themselves to that outcome.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: His earlier model required a much larger equity stake to justify the return. Because some tech companies can reach far bigger exits and need no extra work from him, he can take smaller stakes and invest money only.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: Inbound deal flow came in two buckets: founders with an existing cap table who preferred him as an investor, and bootstrapped founders wanting capital for a clear opportunity. Both need almost no work or expertise from him, provided the deal structure makes sense.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: Demand was high enough and check sizes small enough that he spun ACQ Ventures off and funds deals himself rather than raising a fund. He says it has done roughly six to eight deals in about two months.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: He says his main group operates fully like a private equity group, while ACQ Ventures operates like a VC, run by a general partner from the Y Combinator world who also sources deals independently.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: He looks for businesses that already work and can have gasoline poured on them, rather than ones that only work because of him.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: If a business needs him in order to work, he must keep working until he dies. He cites School, which was compounding monthly with no advertising before he added fuel.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: He solves for revenue retention. If the company dies when the owner goes on vacation, the owner bought a higher-leverage income, not a business, and it is not an asset valuable to others.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: Value to other people is where significant outside returns and wealth creation come from.
title: Why I Started ACQ Ventures

text: He describes a minor league, major league model: people who do well in the minors get promoted to the majors with the team's lead flow, and can drop back if it fails, still receiving services.
title: The Minor League/Major League Model for Scaling a Team

text: Seeing colleagues succeed in the majors gives minor league members an aspirational picture that pushes them to perform better.
title: The Minor League/Major League Model for Scaling a Team

text: As you grow, he suggests adding a JV tier via a new-agent development program, giving three levels (JV, minor, major) with a clean path of ascension between them.
title: The Minor League/Major League Model for Scaling a Team

text: He advises keeping the Zillow-sourced portion of the business at a third or under, because the 40% referral fee comes straight off gross margin and is not expected to fall soon.
title: The Minor League/Major League Model for Scaling a Team

text: In the minor league tier you can cap agents: once they have paid a fixed amount, such as $15,000, to the brokerage, that gives predictable, flat, sticky contributions.
title: The Minor League/Major League Model for Scaling a Team

text: Expansions commonly break because the new market cannot duplicate the current model. He says to pre-fund a local leader who can be trained to duplicate it, rather than expecting the home base to serve it.
title: The Minor League/Major League Model for Scaling a Team

text: He recommends expanding top-down, hiring the leader first, not bottom-up, since new markets have market-specific dynamics that are hard to handle remotely.
title: The Minor League/Major League Model for Scaling a Team

text: Training fails when someone performs many actions and gets feedback only at the end. Hormozi says to interrupt the moment they make a mistake, have them redo it from that point, and correct it on the spot.
title: Helping a Cleaning Business Scale to $3M

text: Hormozi says the training itself can mimic the real workday, such as being on your feet for twelve hours. Those who cannot handle it can then be removed sooner, without wasting more time on them.
title: Helping a Cleaning Business Scale to $3M

text: He says firms like this are usually limited by demand rather than supply, since managing many clients and lots of money takes relatively few resources compared with what they earn. So acquisition is likely the main bottleneck.
title: Helping a $500K Financial Planning Firm Get to $5M

text: He notes that big players run virtual or in-person workshops, because a day or half day builds far more trust than a long stretch online. He would use a workshop as the lead magnet.
title: Helping a $500K Financial Planning Firm Get to $5M

text: He says one of the biggest levers for a fast multiple is at the front: swap the offer from book a call to get a thing, with the call or workshop as its delivery vehicle. He claims this can lift sales from two to eight or ten per month.
title: Helping a $500K Financial Planning Firm Get to $5M

text: He observes that the higher up-market a client is, the less service they tend to need in his experience, and relationship managers can handle many customers.
title: Helping a $500K Financial Planning Firm Get to $5M

text: He states that a business is either a volume player with technology built in from day one and a cost-efficiency model, or a premium player. There is little room in between, and it is hard for people to perceive value there.
title: Helping a $500K Financial Planning Firm Get to $5M

text: He thinks a personal finance offer and an investing offer are different products. Acquiring customers is easier on personal finance, so if that leads to a much higher ascension into wealth management, it can be a great model.
title: Helping a $500K Financial Planning Firm Get to $5M

text: Hormozi thinks it is worth pushing back on the idea that free creators cannot convert, because giving up on them sharply lowers the network's value to sponsors, who pay for impressions those creators can deliver.
title: Helping a $4.3M Creator Platform Business Scale to $100M

text: A platform can pick one of two routes: go high-ticket with premium white-glove onboarding, charging roughly five or ten thousand dollars and only selecting really good creators, or go freemium and treat it as media arbitrage.
title: Helping a $4.3M Creator Platform Business Scale to $100M

text: On the freemium route, you run very large volumes of ads to bring people onto the platform, and you must know your average revenue per platform user.
title: Helping a $4.3M Creator Platform Business Scale to $100M

text: When picking a niche, he says to focus on the avatar you can give the most value to at the lowest possible cost to you; that gap is where the arbitrage occurs.
title: Helping a VA Agency Scale | Hormozi Hotline

text: Customer concentration is not required to pick a niche. What matters is sampling many industries and spotting which ones you can scale faster and which get more value from you.
title: Helping a VA Agency Scale | Hormozi Hotline

text: Illustrative comparison: of three niches, he would pick the middle one, roughly eight times the value for about one and a half times the extra training, over one needing five times the training or one with little value.
title: Helping a VA Agency Scale | Hormozi Hotline

text: A specialized VA agency can standardize training and deliver higher quality from the start, which lets it charge a premium and earn better margins. He says any such specialty could reach 100 million a year.
title: Helping a VA Agency Scale | Hormozi Hotline

text: For niche research with AI, use a prompt chain: ask the AI what questions it needs, answer them, upload that context, ask it to write the prompt for ranking the top five niches by likely return, then run that prompt.
title: Helping a VA Agency Scale | Hormozi Hotline

text: If affiliates are your main way of getting customers, your marketing should target the affiliates, since they are your actual customers, not the end users they serve.
title: Helping a VA Agency Scale | Hormozi Hotline

text: After his team sold eight people into a nonexistent workshop date, they gave gym access, one-on-one advisor time and a dinner, later re-ran the workshop free, believing goodwill like that comes back.
title: Helping a VA Agency Scale | Hormozi Hotline

text: Hormozi says industry averages do not matter to him, because the average business in an industry is poor and does not make money. He would rather judge his own numbers.
title: I've put in my 10,000 hours and I'm not making enough money

text: If a business closes only around 10% of people who come in, Hormozi says the problem is either the sales motion or the offer. If lead costs are too high, he would also examine the offer.
title: I've put in my 10,000 hours and I'm not making enough money

text: Hormozi notes that hiring usually means filling an empty box on the org chart, but people rarely define at a granular level what that person is responsible for. Every business function is really a series of actions.
title: You Need to Stop Being the Bottleneck in Your Business

text: The smallest version of a business's core economic engine is LTV to CAC: money put in returns more money as gross profit, which funds the whole business. At a higher level, the engine is return on invested capital.
title: Helping a $500K Coaching Business Get to $2M

text: His rule of thumb for brick and mortar service businesses is gross margins above 80%, ideally above 90%. He will not run one below 80%, though others do, because there is too little cash to do anything.
title: Helping a $500K Coaching Business Get to $2M

text: He is willing to be a voice for relentless hard work and to sit at the logical extreme, because he thinks the opposite side is wildly over-represented and that this stance will help more people.
title: How To Stop Being Anxious About Your Goals

text: In his experience, more people he has met are dissatisfied with a live-it-up 20s than with a work-it-up 20s.
title: How To Stop Being Anxious About Your Goals

text: In your 20s you usually do not know what you want, but you do know what work moves you ahead. So make progress on the known thing and gain perspective on what truly matters along the way.
title: How To Stop Being Anxious About Your Goals

text: You may find far fewer things matter to you than you first thought. Chasing a living-it-up version shaped by your mom's or mediocre friends' opinions can leave you at 30 having neither lived it up nor worked it up.
title: How To Stop Being Anxious About Your Goals

text: On his first day at university he sat next to his future business partner of 15 years. Having blown his whole term's maintenance loan partying in freshers' week, he was broke by September 29th.
title: How To Stop Being Anxious About Your Goals

text: A pitch that first has to create a problem, then solve it, and also explain an unfamiliar product asks a lot of the prospect. Hormozi would rather talk to people who already know they have the problem.
title: You should start a boring business.

text: Learning a new industry by selling inside it is a good route: pick up the basics, then work out lead generation for it. With lead generation and sales in hand, only delivery remains.
title: You should start a boring business.

text: Insurance sales can be very profitable for someone strong at sales because there is almost no delivery. You sell the product, and large carriers take on the risk.
title: You should start a boring business.

text: Many businesses are demand constrained and have sticky customers. Hormozi suggests finding one you like that serves the customer type you already sell to and know well.
title: You should start a boring business.

text: One way to hire reps with less churn is a try-before-you-buy setup: make them contractors for 30 days, and if they hit the KPIs, roll them in and lock in their base.
title: \"How Do I Hire Better Sales Reps Without Overpaying?\"

text: Alternatively, pay the full base up front and tell the new hire they have 30 days to prove themselves.
title: \"How Do I Hire Better Sales Reps Without Overpaying?\"

text: When judging the risk of a base salary, consider what you actually stand to lose. Paying someone a bad-fit two weeks at roughly 1,000 dollars a week costs about 2,000 dollars.
title: \"How Do I Hire Better Sales Reps Without Overpaying?\"

text: Remote reps compare your offer not just to other jobs in your industry but to all opportunities available to them, so a competitive edge must be judged against that wider field.
title: \"How Do I Hire Better Sales Reps Without Overpaying?\"

text: Demos work in sales because they leave nothing to imagination. He suggests thinking of the offer like an unboxing video that shows what is inside.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: When describing each feature or component of an offer, ask how it helps the buyer avoid pain or gain what they want faster, easier, or with less risk. Risk, speed and ease form the matrix.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: Shoppers on product pages tend to click through all the image tiles, then scan bullets for features, then check price and options, then decide. Good reviews boost this; bad ones hurt.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: Pair the words with visuals: while explaining what is included, show the thing being described so the viewer gets two forms of stimulation at once.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: Each feature or tile will appeal to one specific avatar with one problem in mind, so make sure every relevant problem gets its own tile, and use the text below to add context for readers.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: With few members, run a training or live session on a topic, ask for feedback, and screenshot it to create testimonials matched to each feature tile.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: Copy should move from where the reader is now, to where they want to be, why it matters, then what you do to get them there, and be as tight as possible.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: Test every sentence or bullet by asking whether it lifts the percentage who buy, or brings in a new audience who otherwise would not. The page exists to convert the highest share of desired viewers.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: The headline, first line and PS statement are the most-read parts of almost any sales letter, so add a PS at the end.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: He likes PS statements that say who the offer is not for, since the right people then feel it is for them.
title: Fixing a Relationship Coach's Sales Page

text: A free trial adds a second conversion point: landing page conversion rises, but the step from trial into paid conversion drops. He also notes that churn after a trial tends to be lower than for people who bought outright.
title: The Truth About Free Trials

text: To decide on a trial, build a spreadsheet comparing both paths from 100 clicks: trial rate, trial-to-paid rate, and LTV with each path's churn. Then see which top-line number is higher. He calls it just math.
title: The Truth About Free Trials

text: Trial break-even math: if conversions rose 4x, then when half of trial users cancel you have still doubled sales, when two-thirds cancel you are up 50%, and when three-quarters cancel you are even.
title: The Truth About Free Trials

text: Part of a trial's conversion lift comes from a free call to action pulling more clicks than a buy-now one, so cost per click belongs in the analysis. For organic content, three times the clicks still counts as a gain.
title: The Truth About Free Trials

text: A trial is reversible, so you can always stop it. Running it long enough to get real data means you never have to wonder afterward.
title: The Truth About Free Trials

text: Vague words like mindset or motivation cannot be acted on because nobody can define them. Ask instead which specific activity you feel you should be doing but are not.
title: \"How Do I Become the Next Version of Myself?\"

text: Facing your fears is not a real task, since there is no single ball of fear to confront. There are only specific things you are avoiding, and you should name those actions.
title: \"How Do I Become the Next Version of Myself?\"

text: For outbound, just send the email and call whoever replies. Even a rude response shows you survived, so shrink the gap between fear and action by focusing on activities.
title: \"How Do I Become the Next Version of Myself?\"

text: Split a feared task into small parts, such as filming, writing a caption, pressing send, and checking likes. Find the part that scares you, then ask whether it outweighs helping the people you want to serve.
title: \"How Do I Become the Next Version of Myself?\"

text: At around five million in revenue, hires usually called C-suite are better titled VP or director. He says getting the title right can help when working out their compensation.
title: Helping an Auto Repair Shop Hire Better Talent

text: Before designing a leadership hire, work out which role is actually missing. For an owner-visionary who is the bottleneck on everything operational, the missing piece is an operator acting as a right hand.
title: Helping an Auto Repair Shop Hire Better Talent

text: Equity bundles four things: cash flow, sale proceeds, risk, and control. Employees who say they want equity often want neither risk nor control, so he offers only cash flow and exit upside.
title: Helping an Auto Repair Shop Hire Better Talent

text: He likes profit share pools of roughly 10 to 15 percent, and wants leaders willing to give up part of their own slice because they think the whole pie will grow, which makes them think like owners.
title: Helping an Auto Repair Shop Hire Better Talent

text: Example structure: a phantom profits interest of about 4 percent, vesting 1 percent per year (numbers illustrative). It returns to the company if they leave, and pays out at a sale.
title: Helping an Auto Repair Shop Hire Better Talent

text: He can accelerate the full phantom interest at a sale, but only if the employee is still there during the sale and has served a minimum period such as 12 or 24 months.
title: Helping an Auto Repair Shop Hire Better Talent

text: He describes Reddit as a highly engaged platform with deep attention, high click rates and a lot of trust, beyond ordinary social media, and treats it as one of many places to get traffic.
title: \"How Do I Pick Which Marketing Channel to Advertise On?\"

text: Hormozi says he belongs to a Reddit forum for home gym owners, and that recommendations and full reviews from that community drive real purchases.
title: \"How Do I Pick Which Marketing Channel to Advertise On?\"

text: He says bad word of mouth spreads far more easily than good, putting the ratio of bad to good at about 15 to one, yet few people discuss bad word of mouth going viral.
title: Why Most Coaching Businesses Have to Keep Launching New Offers

text: He argues many coaching-space operators keep launching new offers because their first product was never that good, so they keep hunting for a new thing with a this-time-is-different pitch.
title: Why Most Coaching Businesses Have to Keep Launching New Offers

text: If a business once acquired customers at a fifth of today's price, he says it likely had a mispriced media source or a new acquisition method, and the market later caught up.
title: Why Most Coaching Businesses Have to Keep Launching New Offers

text: He says CAC is fairly comparable across businesses in the same industry, with three to four thousand dollars looking normal in this case. The real gap is LTV, which he thinks should be nearer 20 to 30 thousand.
title: Why Most Coaching Businesses Have to Keep Launching New Offers

text: He tends to fix businesses back to front instead of front to back, since relying on unusually low CAC versus the market is very hard to sustain.
title: Why Most Coaching Businesses Have to Keep Launching New Offers

text: If competitors are still selling to your market profitably, he says it should bother you, since they must have better advertising or bigger LTV, or a mix of both.
title: Why Most Coaching Businesses Have to Keep Launching New Offers

text: He advises prioritizing doubling LTV over cutting CAC in half, describing LTV as the sustainable competitive advantage and CAC as ephemeral.
title: Why Most Coaching Businesses Have to Keep Launching New Offers

text: He believes reaching the highest levels of achievement requires giving up amounts of the very things you hoped the achievement would give you, in proportion to the level reached.
title: I Put On 20 Pounds of Muscle During My Worst Year

text: During 2025 he realized his wealth did not even let him choose his workout length, so he set a rule: he does not train when rushed, and trains as long as needed, even two to three hours.
title: I Put On 20 Pounds of Muscle During My Worst Year

text: He names three things that bring him the most joy: training with someone he likes, eating with someone he likes ideally after training, and writing. He asked why he was sacrificing one of them for success.
title: I Put On 20 Pounds of Muscle During My Worst Year

text: He says that during his worst season, training served as a life raft, and he added about 20 pounds of muscle in 2025 so far. Finishing a strong workout means he has won the day.
title: I Put On 20 Pounds of Muscle During My Worst Year

text: The more skills someone has, the more opportunities they can spot. Disparate skills connect into through lines that people with only one skill cannot see, and a person with one skill has limited options.
title: How to Stack Skills

text: Skills stacked in a related sequence, such as bookkeeping, then accounting, insurance, tax and M&A, together become unbelievably valuable. He says to learn skills that complement each other.
title: How to Stack Skills

text: He questions the Steve Jobs calligraphy story in hindsight, asking whether the Mac would have failed without its fonts. He notes Jobs was deeply into computers and hardware from childhood, and supply chain knowledge would likely have helped that business.
title: How to Stack Skills

text: Across businesses, the product is the real differentiator, while the rest is the same: marketing, sales, HR, legal and finance. Anyone entering the game must learn these functions in addition to knowing the core product deeply.
title: How to Stack Skills

text: Functions must be learned in sequence. Finance cannot come first since there is no money to count yet. You can learn business outside in, starting with promoting and selling, or inside out, starting with building the product.
title: How to Stack Skills

text: Whichever direction you start from, product first or promotion and selling first, you must get deep enough in all three (product, marketing, sales) to earn the first dollar. He says gaps there are the core deficiencies where new business owners struggle.
title: How to Stack Skills

text: When you cannot control price, as with insurance-fixed payments, margin has to come from the cost side. That means running the business very lean, since price is set by someone else.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: Staying in insurance-only practice leads to one of three outcomes: you choose to win at the lean-cost game, a future acquirer imposes it on you, or you eventually burn out.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: If providers are the scarce resource and patient demand is ample, strip out all other costs and shift that money toward providers to attract more of them. He says that is what scales revenue.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: He says insurers price near break-even, just enough for providers to stay barely afloat, so insurance-only operators must be ruthless about numbers.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: Sell toward the goal the patient wants instead of selling a commodity feature such as a single session.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: Intake forms should ask pain-based questions about what the person cannot do because of the problem, rephrasing the same question many ways, rather than generic rating circles.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: A pre-visit video sales letter can cover promise, proof and pain, with examples of common patient types, a four-step plan, and old way versus new way, then answer each common objection with what people think, why it is wrong, and proof.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: Collect ID and a card on file at arrival, before any request for payment, then show a second video with different examples after the exam, before the closer meeting.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: He believes selling the higher-care option alongside insurance may create the margin needed to hire providers, and suggests doubling down on that side once it works.
title: \"I'm Fully Booked. Why Am I Barely Profitable?\"

text: Inside a niche you can charge higher niche prices, your case studies all feel relevant to buyers, and deals come easier. He says this makes pigeonholing less of a real worry.
title: Helping a CFO Turn His Construction Expertise Into a Consulting Business

text: Counterintuitively, a niche can bring more customers than going broad. Advertising to everyone with a gym track record gets fewer gyms than advertising as a gym specialist, and narrower messaging often lifts response rates.
title: Helping a CFO Turn His Construction Expertise Into a Consulting Business

text: He argues that any business, at the top level, is you managing five to seven direct reports such as marketing, sales, HR, legal, IT, finance and customer service. So day-to-day work ends up similar across industries.
title: Helping a CFO Turn His Construction Expertise Into a Consulting Business

text: Hormozi says something should only change your mood if it would change your life. If the cost of something is your peace of mind, he says not to buy it.
title: You're In Control of How Hard Work Feels

text: Avoiding hard tasks because they would make you feel bad is an empty excuse. Since you can have a good day doing unpleasant things, you decide how to perceive your work.
title: You're In Control of How Hard Work Feels

text: He considers choosing how you perceive your work the most freeing tool for getting through harder periods.
title: You're In Control of How Hard Work Feels

text: Better sales performance does not raise LTV; it raises the dollars earned per lead.
title: Helping a $30M Online Service Business Get to $100M

text: For this kind of business at this scale, he thinks a 5 to 1 ratio of lifetime value to acquisition cost is a good target, and fixing sales might get it to roughly 3.5 to 4.
title: Helping a $30M Online Service Business Get to $100M

text: He says the most profitable customers are those who arrive free and those who renew without new acquisition cost; these drop to the bottom line, while everything else in the middle mainly facilitates those two.
title: Helping a $30M Online Service Business Get to $100M

text: Doing identical work for a business making $100 million a year, a 20% bump yields $20 million, and a 10% cut pays him $2 million, versus about $20,000 for a small business. He calls recognizing this a skill.
title: How to Find the Customers Who Value What You Do the Most

text: Hormozi believes solving problems for wealthy people pays better, a point he put in a viral tweet that drew controversy. He restates it as finding the people who value what you offer the most.
title: How to Find the Customers Who Value What You Do the Most

text: He tells a story of a father sending his son to sell an old beat-up car: a dealership offers $1,000, a scrapyard around $500 in metal, and the son is then sent to an antique dealer, showing that value depends on the buyer.
title: How to Find the Customers Who Value What You Do the Most

text: Entering a new market has escalating routes: first face-to-face networking such as conferences and meetups, then digital outreach, which works better with an organic following or as true cold outreach on LinkedIn. Volume is what makes these work.
title: Helping a Real Estate Consultant Get More Leads

text: He would pair a guaranteed path with a fast path: spend roughly 100 to 200 dollars a day on local ads, focus on working those leads and building the sales motion, while still running the normal playbook alongside.
title: Helping a Real Estate Consultant Get More Leads

text: He likes very niche messaging in ads and says being generic realtor number six has no chance. With a unique angle he would be open to Meta as well as LinkedIn.
title: Helping a Real Estate Consultant Get More Leads

text: To decommoditize a service, he would show before-and-afters: what the tenant was first offered, what was negotiated, and the difference.
title: Helping a Real Estate Consultant Get More Leads

text: When savings percentages vary, he would probably express a guarantee or results in dollar amounts if possible.
title: Helping a Real Estate Consultant Get More Leads

text: When about 40% of customers cancel while waiting for delivery, Hormozi says something is wrong with the sale itself, not just with the slow fulfillment.
title: Fixing a Sales Agency With a 40% Cancellation Rate

text: He says the idea that you become the average of your five closest people is incomplete; what matters more is your reference group, meaning who you compare yourself to and whose views you weigh in tough decisions.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: When facing a hard decision, he suggests imagining what people closest to your goal would do and say, rather than consulting the people closest to you physically.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: He thinks proximity has no power on its own; its only value is that it changes your behavior. So the aim is to extract lessons about what you must change in what you do to hit your goals.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: Watching models who succeeded and copying what worked for them is an easy, highly effective way to learn, and many small behaviors get absorbed through observation without the teacher consciously teaching them.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: He says he learned a great deal from his father through years of observation, though often not the lessons his father believed he was teaching. He thinks people learn more from those around them than they let on.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: During private equity talks, he sat at a long table facing a managing partner with a team of VPs and principals, and realized it was obvious why that man would make a billion dollars and he would not.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: He says his company aims to demonstrate excellence rather than just talk about it, because people learn more from small incidental interactions than from any presentation about culture.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: He advises getting into rooms with people above your level whenever possible, focusing on what you need to change in your own behavior. On his way up he did whatever he could to get into every such room.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: He donated 2 million dollars to Arnold's charity to join a board with people who gave over a million each, wanting to see how they talk, think, and prioritize.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: He considers reinvesting in his ability to learn, including paying for access to rooms, probably the best investment of his life, even though the price of those rooms has risen.
title: Change Who You Compare Yourself to

text: Hormozi says he came from a world heavy in franchising and knows several friends who gave away 30% of their business and sold for nine figures to franchise sales organizations.
title: Stop Selling Done-For-You, Sell Franchises Instead

text: He thinks the direct-response world, where people frame everything as offers, is dying. He believes customer acquisition cost is rising and trust is falling, so he does not see it as sustainable long term.
title: Stop Selling Done-For-You, Sell Franchises Instead

text: He believes the coaches are going to fizzle out, and that a person with direct-response skills is applying a viable skill set to the wrong opportunity.
title: Stop Selling Done-For-You, Sell Franchises Instead

text: Software often takes a long time to get right. Ideally it grows organically and compounds by some percentage each month from word of mouth alone, a resting growth rate. Once that exists, you can add paid traffic on top.
title: Helping a $400K SaaS Business Fix Churn

text: Cheap software, such as $50 a month, needs huge traffic volume. If you cannot retain customers or have a viral component replacing those who leave, growth stalls.
title: Helping a $400K SaaS Business Fix Churn

text: Software can grow two ways: accept churn but get more referrals than churn, giving compounding growth, or lose few customers and use built-in expansion revenue so remaining customers spend more and offset losses.
title: Helping a $400K SaaS Business Fix Churn

text: Spending more on marketing is irrelevant if customers all fall out the other side. Until the bucket is fixed, more marketing does not matter, though you can still buy more revenue by marketing more.
title: Helping a $400K SaaS Business Fix Churn

text: A monthly churn of 7% still means losing roughly 60% of customers each year. You can tolerate churn only if referrals exceed it, producing net growth that compounds without advertising.
title: Helping a $400K SaaS Business Fix Churn

text: Free organic impressions are the leverage for a creator-led business. The goal is to make the business grow without them, and only then pour in paid traffic.
title: Helping a $400K SaaS Business Fix Churn

text: Hormozi decided long ago that loyalty was the most important trait in a partner. Expecting many enemies and people wanting to undermine him, he wanted someone he never had to watch his back around.
title: Why I Married Someone a Little Crazy

text: He says he has never doubted his wife's loyalty, not once.
title: Why I Married Someone a Little Crazy

text: Hormozi describes their marriage as very traditional while their business relationship is more modern. He says their working arrangement would look the same even without a romantic relationship, since they learned the work dynamic first.
title: Why I Married Someone a Little Crazy

text: A early mentor advised them to act like business partners, not spouses, in front of their team, since displays of affection make people uncomfortable. They keep affection private and avoid it in public content.
title: Why I Married Someone a Little Crazy

text: They married young, around 23 and 27, with adults working for them, so they felt they needed to be extra professional. Being older now with more gravitas lets them relax somewhat.
title: Why I Married Someone a Little Crazy

text: The faster someone grows, the more they outgrow. There are in-between periods, sometimes lasting years, where you are far ahead of people you know but lack the credibility to join the next group.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: If you keep growing after entering the next group, you eventually pass those people too. Hormozi says from experience that you sometimes have to like your goals more than your friends.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: Whatever you refuse to give up for your goals is something you love more than the goals. The person who beats you is the one who loves their goals more; he says this is neither right nor wrong.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: Much entrepreneur stress comes from judging reality as a problem. One of the fastest ways to solve a problem is to decide it is not one.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: A preference differs from a problem. Wanting more friends does not mean you cannot act without them. If your activities stay the same either way, it is not really a problem.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: Cognitive distortions arise when people attribute causes to things they cannot prove, inserting a narrative such as being stressed because of loneliness. He suggests asking how you know that.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: Test any belief in three steps: how do you know it (logic), what does it mean (define the words, evidence), and who cares (utility, relevance).
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: Lonely is a bucket term for specific behaviors, such as having nobody to call on a Friday. Breaking it into specifics makes it solvable instead of amorphous. He says poor thinking leads to bad decisions.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: Vibe is a bucket for about six behaviors he deems cool. To build a team with great vibes, identify those behaviors and get everyone doing them.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: Being poor and being rich both have problems, and growing and not growing both carry heavy stress. Stress means you are alive, and he says that is okay.
title: \"I Feel Alone as an Entrepreneur\"

text: The Rule of 100 means completing 100 primary actions every day until you reach your goal. The difficult part is working out which actions count as the 100 primary ones.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: In a business, the primary actions are likely some form of promotion, whether to get customers, employees, affiliates, influencers or agencies. Examples include 100 reach outs, 100 minutes of content, or 100 dollars a day on ads.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: Set a kitchen timer, start your day with the 100 actions, and pause the timer whenever you get distracted, drink water or use the bathroom. This shows how long the work truly takes.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: He quotes the idea that fear is a mile wide and an inch deep: it looks like an ocean, but stepping in shows it is shallow.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: Measuring how long your actions take, such as a couple of hours on average, turns vague fear of rejection or bad comments into a known block of time with a finish time.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: He opposes extended morning routines that prepare people to work. He says the best routine is whichever gets you working fastest, since prep only lengthens the time before the work is finished.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: He suggests facing the work itself, detaching from the long-term reward, and tying each session to becoming the person you want to be, like sculpting marble, so each day feels like crafting a masterpiece.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: He is currently focused on defining winning by level of effort: you only win if you leave nothing in the tank. Harder or longer tasks then become chances to empty the tank, and he thinks external winning follows.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: If you do not change your behavior, you learn nothing. When unsure what to do, start first thing with a timer and do not stop until it finishes.
title: How to Take 100 Primary Actions to Reach Your Goal

text: Hormozi says a business cannot really be overextended, but it can be undertalented. Things break when the people brought in during fast growth lack enough skill, so they fall through the cracks.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: The speed of expansion should match the speed at which you can acquire and hire good people. Feeling overextended usually comes from having no capable help.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: Before hiring the next person, make sure the latest hire has become productive. Expansion speed equals your speed at onboarding and activating teammates, moving from training to managing, much like activating a customer.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: For a home service business he would set roughly 30% margin as a minimum target. If it specializes in a niche like heat pumps, he thinks well-run margins could reach 50% or more.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: If you will not raise prices, at least eliminate discounts, and instead offer speed or risk reversal for buying today. With thin margins, discounts of 10 to 15 percent give away half the profit.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: Fear of raising prices comes from believing you sell a commodity. If prospects see you and a rival as the same thing, they pick the cheaper one. Make them perceive the offers as different.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: To escape commodity selling, add speed, add ease, or make the offer more risk-free. Then break the frame by showing the cheap option costs more later, through fixes and delays.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: Pricing is the biggest lever on profit. He cites a meta-analysis mentioned by Patrick Campbell finding it has roughly three to four times the influence of other levers like retention or customer count.
title: How to Know When to Scale Your Service Business

text: Hormozi does not think a business needs a different model to reach a million-plus and go international; he says the route there is building a big brand and a new way of doing business, with pricing and packaging as easy wins.
title: The $100M Service Business Playbook

text: He expects AI-driven delivery in areas like consulting to often keep the same underlying model, since one-on-one consulting has existed for ages; what changes is the delivery vehicle, which gains operating scale, while the business motion stays largely the same.
title: The $100M Service Business Playbook

text: Before deciding between two business models, open the hood and compare the unit economics of each. The larger model may earn more absolute profit while the smaller one wins on return on capital and effort.
title: Helping a Dirt Bike Coach Scale

text: He tells of a brick-and-mortar service business with a micro model and a bigger facility model. The big facilities earned more revenue and absolute profit, but the small ones returned about 5x more on capital and effort.
title: Helping a Dirt Bike Coach Scale

text: Agencies tend to have lower margins and lower valuation multiples because they are so people heavy. He says that is fine, simply a different business model.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: Simple low-risk growth for an agency is to hire the next person. If hiring someone who brings in customers likely yields over 8% more business for the year, that beats other uses of capital.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: A founder has founder magic, so results are disproportionately better when the founder does a function. He expects roughly a 30% performance drop when someone else takes it over, which is fine if built into the financial model.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: Scale to zero means getting the founder's involvement to zero. If any percentage of the business still requires the founder, it does not scale.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: Low-capex businesses like services generally throw off more cash flow than inventory, location or equipment businesses. Service businesses still need capital to grow, just in different ways.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: For service businesses, he names two primary investments with disproportionately high returns: bringing in talent, and brand plays. Squeezing the existing team has limits, so A players unlock more operational capacity.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: Brand plays are big aspirational associations that cement a business as different from competitors. He cites Red Bull's parachute jump from space, and his own book launch as a multi-year bet.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: He is putting roughly six to seven million dollars into his book launch with no clear return he is aware of, viewing it as a multi-year brand bet to draw in people at the edges of his audience.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: Local businesses can still get by longer on Google or Meta ads generating leads. National or international sellers are hit harder by the direct response doom loop; cold ads to a video sales letter for a 10 grand sale with no reputation mostly no longer work.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: The biggest brands that profit from performance marketing spend about 30% of budget on performance and 70% on associations, narrative and founder story. Direct response wins on ROAS at 30 days; branding yields five to twenty times more over 12 months.
title: Helping a marketing agency scale

text: Around age 28 he realized he had long been trying to prove himself to one central person, his father, with whom he barely spoke for five years after he left.
title: What Happens When You Win at the Wrong Game

text: When his father called to apologize for everything, he rejected it rather than accepting it as an olive branch. He now sees that apologies from fathers to sons were not normal in his father's world.
title: What Happens When You Win at the Wrong Game

text: He says the things he is proudest of in himself are the bright side of what once embarrassed him. Being an outcast let him work alone for endless stretches, more than anyone else he knows.
title: What Happens When You Win at the Wrong Game

text: From about age six to sixteen he spent most of his time in his bedroom listening to audio tapes and books, which he links to his ability to outwork others in solitude.
title: What Happens When You Win at the Wrong Game

text: He believes bullying and exclusion sharpened his focus and his ability to read social dynamics, which helped him become one of the UK's best club promoters for about fifteen years.
title: What Happens When You Win at the Wrong Game

text: He admits he cannot split test life, so he cannot know if having friends would have been better. Since his life turned out well, he wants to be genuinely thankful for the past, and says he is still working on that.
title: What Happens When You Win at the Wrong Game

text: Moving from organic, warm traffic to cold paid traffic is an entirely different funnel, so close rates fall; selling roughly one in ten cold leads is normal, and it still works if the math makes sense.
title: \"Should I Build a Coaching Business or an Educational Platform?\"

text: Cold leads are worth pursuing despite lower closing because there are far more of them than warm leads. That volume is the trade-off for lower conversion.
title: \"Should I Build a Coaching Business or an Educational Platform?\"

text: If an owner wants to sell the business eventually, bringing in other personalities beyond the founder is pretty much the route he thinks they will need.
title: \"Should I Build a Coaching Business or an Educational Platform?\"

text: He suggests strongly considering a team of AI avatars, which only became viable in the last year, as the faces for different niches. Build the education once and feed it into them.
title: \"Should I Build a Coaching Business or an Educational Platform?\"

text: He sees an AI avatar business as removing people risks: avatars do not cheat, sleep, or leave to work for a competitor.
title: \"Should I Build a Coaching Business or an Educational Platform?\"

text: Avatars can be modeled on people you know by licensing their likeness, or created entirely from scratch; he says either approach works.
title: \"Should I Build a Coaching Business or an Educational Platform?\"

text: To improve conversion, inspect every conversion point in the process, not just pickup and closed deal. Tweak a few things at each step, then add up the percentage gains across steps.
title: Helping a Real Estate Company Scale Their Marketing

text: Advanced businesses differ from beginner ones mainly because they do the basics without messing them up, and they do it at scale, rather than adding fancy tactics.
title: Helping a Real Estate Company Scale Their Marketing

text: Solo operators or tiny teams are usually profitable because the owner does everything right. Trouble starts when hired people are poorly trained and not incentivized; doing what worked, at scale, would make a business very advanced.
title: Helping a Real Estate Company Scale Their Marketing

text: Find what frustrates customers in the process, pick the problems you can control, put hard costs on solving them, and wrap those solutions into the offer to make it irresistible.
title: Helping a Real Estate Company Scale Their Marketing

text: Asking a prospect whether others discussed the extra costs they will face makes you sound more educated than competitors, who he says are lazy about it. Covering those costs in your offer helps you win.
title: Helping a Real Estate Company Scale Their Marketing

text: When unsure about marrying Leila, a mentor told him to look at his stats: business up, eating and exercise better, less stress, all thanks to the space she created. That made the decision easier.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He thinks many people chase fireworks rather than a slow-heating furnace that lasts through good and bad times; if a match makes sense without emotion, it will still make sense when emotion fades.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: Falling in love is like dosing yourself for roughly 6 to 24 months, during which you cannot trust your own judgment. So make the decision as rationally as possible up front.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He notes that delaying marriage and kids ignores biology, which has not kept pace with culture; if you want several kids, the window is small.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He prefers dealing with reality as it is, rather than betting on a hoped-for future solution while knowingly paying a near-certain price.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He thinks the best thing a partner can do is help you become your best self, and other friends can fulfill other needs.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He rejects the soulmate idea and the fallacy of the perfect pick. Ask whether the person will make you better or hold you back, and whether you share non-negotiables like kids and travel.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: Leila was 23 and he was 26 when she watched him lose everything twice before they married, so he felt confident she liked him for himself.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He says his relationship with Leila is very traditional, and that very strong women need an even stronger man.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He advises younger men to find a competent wife, since incentives then take care of themselves, and says marriage makes you more money by freeing time otherwise spent dating.
title: Brutally Honest Advice for Relationships

text: He says a campaign cannot be judged unless you are willing to spend about twice your target CAC on the test. With a 2K target CAC, spending under 4K teaches you almost nothing.
title: Helping a Fitness Coach Agency Get to $1M per Month

text: Testing needs a budget above target CAC because feedback at low spend arrives too slowly. Expecting the first attempt to be efficient is unlikely, so you must fund the tuning period.
title: Helping a Fitness Coach Agency Get to $1M per Month

text: He found that marketing directly to small businesses was hard, so he marketed to agencies that served them instead and offered to handle the work they did not want to do.
title: Helping a Fitness Coach Agency Get to $1M per Month

text: He would test several hooks and expects one to work, then scale it once known. Examples: tired of clients leaving after three months, or recurring revenue from every customer you ever sold.
title: Helping a Fitness Coach Agency Get to $1M per Month

text: In his earlier business, an agency cost about 5,000 to acquire, paid 25,000 to onboard, about 1,000 per end customer (for example 50 customers meant 50,000), plus recurring around 30% of top line.
title: Helping a Fitness Coach Agency Get to $1M per Month

text: He warns that going one level up means serving two customer groups, needing a customer success manager for the intermediaries and success on the end-customer side too.
title: Helping a Fitness Coach Agency Get to $1M per Month

text: Hormozi describes two ways to operate in a business: managers, whose best day is packed with contacts and decisions across departments, and makers, whose best day is completely empty. Conflict arises because managers must still talk to makers.
title: How To Be So Productive It Feels Like Cheating

text: Deep work usually needs about 30 to 45 minutes to reach flow, and an upcoming meeting acts as an open loop that pulls attention away beforehand. So a ten-minute manager meeting can cost a maker half a day.
title: How To Be So Productive It Feels Like Cheating

text: When he had little money and only time, he did maker work from 4 a.m. to 9 a.m. and expected fires afterward. With more skilled people and leverage, he pushed that boundary toward noon.
title: How To Be So Productive It Feels Like Cheating

text: For roughly five years his cadence was working from about 5 a.m. to noon or 1 p.m., then holding meetings once tired, since meetings need less horsepower than creative deep work.
title: How To Be So Productive It Feels Like Cheating

text: He now gets an energizing feeling from an empty day, and says going from zero to one meeting roughly halves his subjective wellbeing for that day. He tells his team any meeting must be priced as a whole day.
title: How To Be So Productive It Feels Like Cheating

text: Almost nothing in business is truly urgent, though many things are important. A payment processor shutting down is urgent, but even a lawsuit is not, since a response takes time. He says executives and assistants must be taught this.
title: How To Be So Productive It Feels Like Cheating

text: His media presence serves to generate demand, feeding people onward: those wanting to start a business go to school, those growing modestly go to advisory, pure tech companies go to ventures, and larger companies go to private equity.
title: How To Be So Productive It Feels Like Cheating

text: Niching should solve a real problem, not be done for its own sake. A niche can allow more specific messaging and a higher lifetime value to acquisition cost ratio, which in theory lets you expand.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: If delivery differs a lot between business types, niching makes sense because you can productize, use templates and streamline the back end.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: Niching is an efficiency fix: when nobody responds to ads, pick the most profitable existing customers and tailor the offer and lead magnet to them. This raises lifetime gross profit per customer and, with targeting, lowers acquisition cost.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: He says a company can rest on two things: people who never stop buying and people who never stop selling for you. Having both makes a wonderful business.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: Ask what the irresistible offer to an affiliate is. A standard 20% referral commission usually gets no referrals, and he says it has to be irresistible for the program to work.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: One way to make an affiliate offer irresistible is letting partners include your service, or a portion of it, in their own services at no added cost to them.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: He suggests re-engaging existing partners and integrating into their customer journey, since relying on them to remember you is not enough. The goal is that every customer they sell gets something from you, creating upsell chances.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: A friend's CPA firm sets up an LLC and first bank account free for new small businesses, normally about $300, because he upsells bookkeeping for $2,000 a year. Partners bundle this in and book calls with him.
title: The Irresistible Referral Offer That Makes Partners Sell for You Without Asking

text: He thinks the dead internet theory has effectively already happened, because most people repeat ideas they did not originate and cannot explain, behaving like robots.
title: How to Know Which of Your Beliefs Are Actually Yours

text: If you cannot explain why you believe something, it is not really your belief but someone else's. People will defend borrowed beliefs yet resist accepting a belief from the person they are talking to.
title: How to Know Which of Your Beliefs Are Actually Yours

text: When someone disagrees with you, ask yourself what if they are right. He suggests this quick check to avoid treating disagreement as an attack on your worth.
title: How to Know Which of Your Beliefs Are Actually Yours

text: In high school he was strongly pro affirmative action but had to argue the opposite side in a class debate. Afterward he concluded he had been wrong and that it hurts more than it helps.
title: How to Know Which of Your Beliefs Are Actually Yours

text: In the gym world he judged others' training, then learned they were right, then later that his original view mattered, then more. After several flips he concluded all methods hit a genetic max and differ only in speed.
title: How to Know Which of Your Beliefs Are Actually Yours

text: After being wrong several times in a row, he decided to be humble and train the way he enjoys, since he likes it and it brings him joy.
title: How to Know Which of Your Beliefs Are Actually Yours

text: He likes a phrase he saw on a yacht name: do not analyze your pleasures. He thinks judge is the better word; if something feels good, do not question it, just enjoy it.
title: How to Know Which of Your Beliefs Are Actually Yours

text: AI output only sounds like generic AI when it has no baseline of your own work. Trained on work you have already done, it produces output that sounds like that work.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: Think leverage and amplification, not automation. True automation would run forever, never break and keep improving, which is rare; realistically AI gives more leverage, not infinite leverage.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: Tasks he says he does faster with AI: emails went from 60 to 90 minutes down to 15 to 20, tweets from about 90 minutes a day to about 90 minutes a week, YouTube videos from 2 hours to 15 minutes.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: Pure AI-generated tweets copy-pasted do not work for him; AI helps by giving inspiration and ideas to iterate on, and he still edits heavily.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: You are rewarded for work you have already done: his tweets and emails are strong because he fed in thousands of his own earlier tweets and emails as a data source.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: The idea is the leverage. AI cannot have real-life experience, so the core idea, learnings and stories must come from you; AI can flesh them out.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: AI is currently more a remixer than original. It is good at replicating format, structure, sentence patterns and language, while the core value must come from you.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: A beginner churning out AI content does not win, having no experience or ideas; you must do things and then talk about them, and AI lets you talk about more of it faster.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: Three ingredients for AI to work: complete business context, an SOP repository, and data sources of past work. Separate assets clearly, for example transcripts divided by markers, then upload them.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: To build a sales script, feed several winning call transcripts and instruct it to keep only lines appearing in multiple winning calls, remove filler, use simple language, and keep the pitch under five minutes.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: Asking AI to just write newsletters will produce poor results; give it the core idea or story and a template, and instruct it to learn style, not copy phrasing.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: Do not just say sound like me. Give machine-like, specific style instructions on sentence length, rhythm, syntax, punctuation, diction and devices, which a machine can hold in mind better than a human.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: Managers can feed sales call transcripts to AI for feedback as a master salesperson, then use it in one-on-ones and role-play; reps can also get their own feedback.
title: How to use AI to grow your business

text: For lead magnets that do not produce booked calls, ask AI to build a follow-up sequence of SMS and email tailored to that specific lead magnet.
title: How to use AI to grow your business
